Topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

Target audience: University students (Calculus I)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Review: The Rate of Change

Lecture lines:
The derivative measures the instantaneous rate of change.
Visualize this as a speedometer at one frozen moment.
It captures the slope of f(x) at point x.

Planned animations:
Fade in Rate of Change symbol (dR/dt) in #FFFFFF color.
Animate a tangent line sliding along a curve.
Highlight the slope value changing at each point.
Draw a small triangle under the tangent line.
Label the rise and run in #FFCC00 color.

Section: section_2 — The Conceptual Shift: Accumulation

Lecture lines:
Integration calculates the area under a curve.
It accumulates tiny slices to form a total.
Think of it as the sum of growth segments.

Planned animations:
Display an area region under a curve in #3399FF.
Flash the accumulation growth as x increases.
Highlight total sum of thin rectangles under curve.

Section: section_3 — The Fundamental Theorem (Visualizing the Link)

Lecture lines:
The Fundamental Theorem connects these two operations.
They are inverse processes acting on functions.
A scanner reveals how one rebuilds the other.
Derivative deconstructs growth into instantaneous rates.
Integral reconstructs the total from those rates.

Planned animations:
Place F(x) formula in #FFFFFF on the left.
Place integral of f(t)dt in #FFFFFF on right.
Show the link arrow between them in #FF3366.
Highlight the shared variable 'x' in both.
Zoom in on the final equivalence equation.

Section: section_4 — The Core Connection: Cancellation

Lecture lines:
Differentiating an integral recovers the original function.
The process effectively undoes the integration.
It is a perfect mathematical cancellation.

Planned animations:
Visualize f(x+h) - f(x) as a gap.
Show how the integral fills this gap.
Highlight the cancelation of terms in purple #AA33FF.

Section: section_5 — Synthesis & Summary

Lecture lines:
Differentiation and integration are linked inverses.
They represent the cycle of rates and accumulation.
Mastery allows navigation between these two worlds.

Planned animations:
Group all fundamental theorem components on screen.
Briefly flash the relationship arrows again.
Fade out everything to black screen finish.

from manim import *

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        return mobject

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Summary", [
            "Differentiation and integration are linked inverses.",
            "They represent the cycle of rates and accumulation.",
            "Mastery allows navigation between these two worlds."
        ])
        
        # Create visual elements
        # Representing "Differentiation" and "Integration" as nodes
        diff_node = Circle(radius=0.7, color=BLUE).add(Text("d/dx", font_size=20))
        int_node = Circle(radius=0.7, color=GREEN).add(Text("∫", font_size=30))
        
        # Arrows representing the link
        arrow1 = CurvedArrow(start_point=LEFT, end_point=RIGHT, angle=-PI/2, color=YELLOW)
        arrow2 = CurvedArrow(start_point=RIGHT, end_point=LEFT, angle=-PI/2, color=YELLOW)
        
        visuals = VGroup(diff_node, int_node, arrow1, arrow2)
        self.place_in_area(visuals, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(visuals))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(Indicate(visuals))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeOut(visuals))
        self.wait(1)
